description: Create, edit and delete rows over a server-side row model in a Svelte 5 data grid, against a backend that validates and refuses. A new order goes in through the edit panel under the focused region and lands as a transaction; an inline edit is one updateRow that carries the row version, so an edit that lost a race to another user is refused with a conflict; a delete of a shipped order is refused; a delete that went through can be undone. The saving flag shows while a write is in flight. Optimistic mode shows the edit before the server answers and restores the row when the server refuses; the slow-server switch makes the difference visible. The write log shows what the server received and what it said.
keywords: svelte 5 data grid create update delete server
svelte grid optimistic update rollback server row model
svelte grid edit conflict version check

faq.question: What happens when the server refuses an edit?
faq.answer: updateRow rejects with the server's message. Waiting for the server, the cell never changed, so nothing moves; in optimistic mode the model had already shown the new value and puts the previous row back. The demo logs the refusal and shows it in the footer.

faq.question: How does the demo detect that someone else edited the row?
faq.answer: Every row carries a version. The inline edit sends the version the grid read the row at; the mock server compares it with the one it holds and refuses the write when they differ, the way a real backend does with a version column or an updated_at check. Reload group re-reads the level in place so the next edit carries the current version.

faq.question: Where does a new row land?
faq.answer: createRow(values, route) writes through the datasource and applies the saved row as a transaction under the route, here the region the form was seeded with from the focused row, so the row appears without refetching the level; the top level is refreshed in place so the region subtotals and counts follow.
